title: Principality of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
capsule: The Principality of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen was a sovereign German state in the upper Danube Valley of Swabia, ruled by the Catholic southern branch of the Hohenzollern dynasty. It entered the Confederation of the Rhine under French protection in 1806, gaining princely status, and became a member of the German Confederation in 1815 after the Napoleonic Wars. During the revolutions of 1848, Prince Karl abdicated under popular pressure; his son Karl Anton sought Prussian military assistance, and Prussian troops arrived in August 1849. By a treaty formalized in December 1849 and taking effect in March 1850, the principality was annexed to Prussia and became part of the new Province of Hohenzollern. Karl Anton later served as Prussian Minister-President (1858–1861), and his son Karl became Carol I of Romania, founding a dynasty that lasted until 1947.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's territory and political history are well-documented in German confederation records and Prussian archives; boundaries are clearly defined. The dataset to-date of 1853 appears to reflect a lag before official Prussian administrative integration was completed.
